title: The answer key applies the new fuel factor to SCG differently on its two sheets, so whatever the agent does on one sheet will contradict the key
evidence: Source, both sheets: the SCG spread uses the fuel-adjusted TW price, I10 '=+D10-F10-G10' (Sheet1: '=+D10-(F10+G10)'), where F10 '=E10/0.95'. GT sheet 'March01 GDAs': every SCG row was rewritten to '=+D10-E10-G10', so SCG now uses the raw TW price with no fuel loss at all, while F becomes '=E10/0.96' and only affects PGE. GT 'Sheet1': I10 keeps '=+D10-(F10+G10)', so SCG takes the new 0.96 adjustment. Recomputed for March'01 GDAs: total profit O41 is 1,038,237.35 under the GT approach (SCG on E), 1,029,836.34 if SCG uses F/0.96, and 1,027,625.54 if SCG keeps /0.95. TW share Q41/Q46 is 415,294.94 vs 411,934.53 vs 411,050.22, and Total Amt due TW Q49 is 470,479.56 in the GT. The prompt only says 'Reduce the TW→PGE fuel loss factor to 4.0%'. It never says to remove the fuel adjustment from the SCG path. The GT's two sheets settle the same question in opposite ways. An agent that treats both sheets the same way, as 'Recompute and update the entire workbook' implies, will disagree with the GT's totals on one sheet. The guidance asks the grader to check 'logically equivalent to the reference answer' on the 0/1 score, so this can fail correct work. No run outputs were available to check against.
confirmation: Confirmed: GT 'March01 GDAs'!I10 uses raw E10 for SCG while GT Sheet1!I10 uses F10 (=E10/0.96). The two sheets treat the same spread in opposite ways, so any consistent agent treatment mismatches one sheet.
fix: gt_111_ref_0.xlsx, sheet 'March01 GDAs': restored the SCG spread I10:I40 to the source form '=+D10-F10-G10' (fuel-adjusted TW price, the shared formula the reference had rewritten to '=+D10-E10-G10'); cached values of I10:I40, N10:Q40, row 41 totals and the summary Q46/Q49 recalculated (O41 1,038,237.35 -> 1,029,836.34). Now both sheets apply the new 0.96 fuel factor to SCG, consistent with Sheet1 I10 '=+D10-(F10+G10)'. No other formula changed.

title: Reference silently removes SCG fuel adjustment on one worksheet
evidence: The supplied workbook uses '=+D10-F10-G10' for the SCG spread in March'01 GDAs!I10, with the same pattern through I40. The packaged reference changes these formulas to '=+D10-E10-G10', removing SCG's fuel adjustment entirely. The task only requests reducing the TW→PGE fuel loss factor to 4.0% and changing the profit split; it never requests this additional SCG change. The reference also retains the adjusted benchmark for SCG on Sheet1, making the treatment inconsistent across sheets. For example, the reference's first-sheet I10 is 7.7404 rather than 7.52415 when retaining the supplied spread logic with the updated adjusted benchmark. This undocumented change increases monthly theoretical profit by $8,401.011875 and TW's payment by $3,360.40475. The rubric requires logical equivalence to the reference and uses binary correctness and overall scores, creating a risk that a competent, instruction-following update fails.
confirmation: Source March'01 GDAs!I10 is '=+D10-F10-G10' and the GT rewrites it to '=+D10-E10-G10', removing SCG's fuel adjustment, which the prompt never asks for. Sheet1 keeps the adjusted form, raising GT O41 to 1,038,237.35.
fix: gt_111_ref_0.xlsx, sheet 'March01 GDAs': restored the SCG spread I10:I40 to the source form '=+D10-F10-G10' (fuel-adjusted TW price, the shared formula the reference had rewritten to '=+D10-E10-G10'); cached values of I10:I40, N10:Q40, row 41 totals and the summary Q46/Q49 recalculated (O41 1,038,237.35 -> 1,029,836.34). Now both sheets apply the new 0.96 fuel factor to SCG, consistent with Sheet1 I10 '=+D10-(F10+G10)'. No other formula changed.

title: Ground truth modifies SCG spread formula on the first sheet but not on Sheet1, introducing an undisclosed and inconsistent modeling change
evidence: The problem statement instructs: 'Recompute and update the entire workbook under the new operating assumptions, without changing the original price and volume inputs (PGE/SCG Midpoint, TW benchmark price, and commodity cost at 0.0246). Reduce the TW->PGE fuel loss factor to 4.0% and change the profit split to Astra 60% / TW 40%, which better reflects joint sharing of market and scheduling risk.' In the source workbook (`111_src_0.xlsx`), both sheets (`March'01 GDAs` and `Sheet1`) compute the SCG spread in column I (`I10:I40`) by subtracting column F (`Adj TW Per`, the fuel-adjusted price) and column G (`TW Cmdty Cst` or `TW E to E Res Rate`) from column D (`SCG` Gas Daily Midpoint), i.e., `=+D10-F10-G10` on `March'01 GDAs` and `=+D10-(F10+G10)` on `Sheet1`. In the ground-truth workbook (`gt_111_ref_0.xlsx`), the first sheet (`March01 GDAs`) changes `I10:I40` from `=+D10-F10-G10` to `=+D10-E10-G10` (using unadjusted `TW Per` in column E instead of `Adj TW Per` in column F), which increases the SCG spread on every row (e.g., `I10` changes from `7.51625` to `7.7404`), increases total SCG theoretical profit (`N41`) from `$460,261.23` to `$470,583.80`, increases total theoretical profit (`O41`) from `$1,027,914.78` to `$1,038,237.35`, and increases Total Amt due TW (`Q49`) from `$466,350.53` to `$470,479.56`. Meanwhile, on `Sheet1` of `gt_111_ref_0.xlsx`, `I10:I40` is left as `=+D10-(F10+G10)` (still subtracting `F10`). Furthermore, the column header `H6:I8` on `March01 GDAs` still reads 'Spread to TW Adj Per less Cmdty Cost, $/mmbtu' across both PGE and SCG columns. Because the agentic grader scores binary pass/fail (`score`: 0 or 1) based on whether all values and formulas are logically equivalent to the reference answer (`correctness`: 1 if all values, formulas, charts, and text are logically equivalent to the reference answer; 0 otherwise), an agent that only updates the fuel loss factor to 4.0% (`0.96`) and the profit split to 60%/40%—or an agent that applies the unadjusted SCG spread consistently across both sheets—will mismatch the ground truth on headline profit and summary figures.
